summary: The old harness has two independent, preexisting compile blockers. The diff also adds pretty formatting behavior for empty objects and arrays that this harness cannot reach.

coverage_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the old entry's calls and lifetime.

claims.necessity_reason: The complete entry declares obj but passes jobj to object iteration. Neither version's iteration macro supplies that argument; the C++ target cannot compile this existing operation.

before.requirement: Compile the entry's object iteration with a declared object argument.
before.reason: The entry passes jobj, while its parsed object is named obj.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The iteration macro uses its supplied object argument.

after.requirement: Compile the entry's object iteration with a declared object argument.
after.reason: The same jobj argument remains in the unchanged entry.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The unchanged iteration macro uses its supplied object argument.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The recipe compiles this entry as C++.

claims.comparison_reason: The same undeclared argument blocks the same existing operation on both sides.

claims.necessity_reason: The entry passes two arguments to a function declared with one argument on both sides, preventing its existing serialization call from compiling.

before.requirement: Invoke json_object_to_json_string with its declared one-argument signature.
before.reason: The old call supplies obj and a flags expression.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The implementation also takes one argument.

after.requirement: Invoke json_object_to_json_string with its declared one-argument signature.
after.reason: The signature and the old two-argument call are unchanged.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The unchanged implementation takes one argument.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The recipe compiles the call as C++.

claims.comparison_reason: The same argument-count mismatch blocks serialization before and after.

claims.necessity_reason: The changed object formatter supports one-line braces for an empty object under pretty formatting. The entry attempts pretty serialization of parsed objects, but its existing compile blockers prevent any input from reaching that behavior.

before.requirement: Reach one-line pretty serialization of an empty object.
before.reason: Before the change, the formatter adds a newline immediately after the opening brace when PRETTY is set.

after.requirement: Reach one-line pretty serialization of an empty object from a valid input such as {}.
after.reason: The formatter now adds pretty newlines only while processing children or after children existed; the old entry cannot compile its serialization call.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parsing an opening brace constructs an object.

claims.comparison_reason: The one-line empty-object behavior is added after the change; the old entry's serialization call prevents reaching it.

claims.necessity_reason: The changed array formatter supports one-line brackets for an empty array under pretty formatting. The entry attempts pretty serialization of parsed arrays, but its existing compile blockers prevent any input from reaching that behavior.

before.requirement: Reach one-line pretty serialization of an empty array.
before.reason: Before the change, the formatter adds a newline immediately after the opening bracket when PRETTY is set.

after.requirement: Reach one-line pretty serialization of an empty array from a valid input such as [].
after.reason: The formatter now adds pretty newlines only while processing elements or after elements existed; the old entry cannot compile its serialization call.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Parsing an opening bracket constructs an array.

claims.comparison_reason: The one-line empty-array behavior is added after the change; the old entry's serialization call prevents reaching it.

missing_information: For complete target-call-path coverage, supply json_object_to_json_string_ext in json_object.c and the JSON_OBJECT_NEW callback setup in json_object.c.
For complete included-header coverage, supply json.h.cmakein and the JSON_C_TO_STRING_PRETTY and JSON_C_TO_STRING_SPACED definitions in json_object.h.
